panels.title: PAYDAY
panels.narration: Your payday arrives. It is a jar. Excellent liquidity.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: The one worker deflates while the one scribe points to the ordinary record; no unsupported first-prize claim.

panels.comic_expression: Wide-eyed surprise becomes an absurdly professional nod.

panels.title: SMALL PRINT
panels.narration: A paycheck? Easy. Proving history’s first? Less easy.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Medium reaction: the worker holds the giant jar and starts to celebrate, but the scribe raises a skeptical finger and produces a plainly BLANK small clay tablet. Worker freezes midway through a grin, one eyebrow absurdly raised. Setup versus doubt, not a coronation. Jar right, the two human faces central.

panels.comic_expression: One eyebrow snaps upward; the wing slowly lowers.

panels.title: MESOPOTAMIA
panels.narration: Mesopotamia. More than five thousand years ago. Bring a cup.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: WIDE establishing of the two familiar men in the mudbrick settlement: worker proudly brings an absurdly TINY plain clay cup toward the GIANT jar on the counter; scribe looks back and forth between cup and jar, completely deadpan. Emphasize the mismatch of scale, no implied historical volume. Funny tiny cup prominent foreground.

panels.comic_expression: Deadpan scale comparison; no historical quantity is implied.

panels.title: THE RECEIPT
panels.narration: This British Museum tablet records beer allocated to workers.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Tight medium action on the scribe presenting a large plain reddish clay accounting tablet with both hands, while worker catches and steadies the wobbly slab on the counter. Exaggerated alarm face and sweat, torso leaning in, tablet at center-right. Tablet remains completely BLANK; it is a reconstruction prop, not a generated artifact transcription.

panels.comic_expression: The grand reveal ends with a practical little adjustment.

panels.title: RATIONS
panels.narration: Daily rations, specifically. Civilization brought its own paperwork.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: The worker recoils as the scribe stacks another plain clay accounting tablet on an absurdly tall wobbling paperwork pile beside a beer jar. The worker's eyes bulge, one hand braces the pile, the other holds a tiny cup; scribe is cheerfully oblivious. Keep all clay slabs BLANK, no ancient script or modern papers.

panels.comic_expression: Dry bureaucratic exasperation; the extra props are a comic metaphor.

panels.title: THE DATE
panels.narration: Between thirty-one hundred and three thousand BC, says the museum.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Scribe tries to straighten an entirely BLANK rectangular teaching board on a plain wooden support at right; worker points irritably as the board tilts in the other direction. Their comic expressions show petty disagreement during a serious date explanation. Keep a clear cream empty rectangle in the board centered around x1400 y500 for program-drawn date; the board contains absolutely NO letters or numerals.

panels.comic_expression: A serious fact delivered during a petty fight with the caption.

panels.title: KEEP THE RECEIPT
panels.narration: That is a very long time to keep receipts.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Worker tries to file an oversized clay tablet into a comically TINY reed basket, knees bent and elbows straining; scribe measures the mismatch with his fingers and gives a very unimpressed side-eye. Tablet and basket make contact and jam visibly. All blank clay, no filing cabinet or modern furniture.

panels.comic_expression: One unhurried blink after a quick failed attempt.

panels.title: A JAR SIGN
panels.narration: The beer sign represents a jar. Branding: aggressively literal.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Scribe presents an entirely BLANK cream teaching board at the RIGHT, indicating it with an overconfident lecturer finger. Worker at left compares an ordinary terracotta jar with the blank board, eyes narrowed in sarcastic recognition. Board blank interior occupies right half (approximately x1125..1775 y335..725 after export), ready for software schematic; NO DRAWN glyph inside.

panels.comic_expression: The crow looks from jar to diagram and gives a tiny exhausted nod.

panels.title: CONTENTS INCLUDED
panels.narration: Its wavy lines show beer inside. Helpful accounting.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Worker peers dramatically inside a plain open terracotta jar, eyebrows raised in discovery; scribe points dryly from the jar to a wholly BLANK cream teaching board on the RIGHT. Different pose/composition from the prior lecture. Board interior right half clear (x1125..1775 y335..725), no letters, waves, signs or diagrams yet; software adds those.

panels.comic_expression: An exaggerated recognition reaction; no claim of an exact transcription.

panels.title: THREE SIGNS
panels.narration: The sign appears three times. Count symbols, not drinks.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Worker at LEFT emphatically raises exactly THREE fingers with a smug counting face; scribe gives him an exhausted sideways stare. Three small entirely blank clay tokens/cards sit on the counter, separate from a single jar. Entire right upper/central region stays pale and clear for a program-drawn diagram. No counted drink glasses, no numbers or generated symbols.

panels.comic_expression: A rapid correction, not a drinking action or a consumption claim.

panels.title: BOWL AND HEAD
panels.narration: Another sign connects a bowl and a human head.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Worker at LEFT holds a plain clay BOWL toward his mouth while scribe gently redirects his head toward a completely BLANK cream board at RIGHT, teaching a visual connection between eating and records. Worker makes an exaggerated bewildered face, scribe patient deadpan. Board blank center x1125..1775 y335..725; no ancient glyph or drawn diagram inside.

panels.comic_expression: A visual explanation with a reaction; the head is a diagram, not a new speaking character.

panels.title: READ THE RECORD
panels.narration: It means eating. We are reading a ration record.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Worker reaches eagerly toward a simple bowl of food, but the scribe slides a large plain clay accounting record into the foreground between the bowl and the viewer. Worker pauses with a magnificent disappointed expression, scribe gives a dry knowing smile. The joke is the distinction between the meal and its record, not eating clay. Blank clay tablet, fully clothed characters.

panels.comic_expression: An overly grand bow for a mundane administrative discovery.

panels.title: NO FIRST PRIZE
panels.narration: A record, not proof of humanity’s very first wage.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: The one worker deflates while the one scribe points to the ordinary record; no unsupported first-prize claim.

panels.comic_expression: Celebration denied by the evidence, with a perfectly straight face.

panels.title: NO MAGIC NUMBER
panels.narration: No universal litres per worker can be read from that.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Worker confronts several comically different-sized plain clay cups and reaches for an absurdly large one; the scribe blocks his arm with an unmistakable STOP gesture and an exasperated face. A single jar and completely blank clay record nearby. This is a joke against inferring a universal measured ration: no ruler, no modern numeric measurement, no litre labels, no quantities or text.

panels.comic_expression: A firm librarian stare; no invented ration appears even as a gag.

panels.title: BEER AND BUREAUCRACY
panels.narration: Beer. Workers. Paperwork. The real story is already absurd enough.

action.start: The recurring human worker and scribe enact the cited comic setup.
action.resolution: Final comic payoff: worker struggles to balance a huge beer jar while several blank clay accounting tablets tip toward him; scribe catches the top tablet with one hand, still wearing an absurdly professional deadpan smile. Both humans clearly acting, funny diagonal pile, strong poses, contact, motion lines, no crow. Keep the lower-left small corner relatively clear for a separate narrator inset NOT drawn into this art.

panels.comic_expression: A quick physical payoff followed by a deadpan stare into camera.

production_trials.animation_limit: Human-only native illustrations with continuous comic punch-ins and bounded shake; fourteen 0.15-second FFmpeg xfades; small separate plaque-free presenter in c01/c15 only. Camera animation, not articulated limb animation.
